description: Dispatch an async job that queries actual lead records by an instance-supported filter_type and up to 300 filter_values, and return {job_id, status} in milliseconds -- the query itself, including Marketo's internal 300-per-call vendor pagination up to the effective row limit, runs in a background worker. Poll check_marketo_job_status(job_id) for the finished result: path, columns, row_count, and truncated. Read describe_lead_fields.searchable_fields first to discover valid standard and custom filter types. Defaults to 500 rows to avoid exhausting vendor rate limits and disk, and to discourage pulling all records for client-side filtering a vendor query should do instead. To fetch more, pass acknowledge_default_limit_override=true together with an explicit row_limit (up to 5,000) -- both required together, refused rather than clamped above 5,000, and refused at DISPATCH time (before any job is created), not discovered later on the finished job. Beyond the hard cap there is no resumption: re-invoke with a narrower filter_values slice (e.g. a 45,000-lead job needs several non-overlapping calls, ~17 internal vendor calls each) -- check get_api_usage first if the daily quota is a concern for a large pull. Optional fields restricts returned columns -- prefer requesting stable ID and status fields over email, phone, or address fields when the goal is validation rather than a task that genuinely needs them.
embedding_description: Query actual Marketo lead (person) records -- names, emails, custom fields -- by matching a searchable field against up to 300 values. Async: a background job builds a workspace TSV of matching people while dispatch returns a job_id in milliseconds; retrieve the finished export with check_marketo_job_status. Prefer stable ID fields over PII for validation.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dict with job_id (pass to check_marketo_job_status to retrieve the finished export) and status (always 'queued' -- this verb never waits for the vendor fetch).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Confirm the job was dispatched and give the job_id; tell the caller to poll check_marketo_job_status(job_id) for the finished TSV handle (path, row_count, columns, truncated). Do not claim the leads have been fetched yet -- this response only confirms the fetch STARTED.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Never report lead data, a row_count, or a file path from THIS verb's response -- it never carries them. Those only appear once check_marketo_job_status reports status=completed.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Validate the lead-query request and dispatch a background job to fetch the matching leads and write them to a tab-separated file in the operator's workspace, up to an acknowledged override ceiling. This verb only validates and dispatches -- it never talks to Marketo directly.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: These are DISPATCH-time errors only -- caught before any vendor call is made, so no job was created. marketo.invalid_params: missing filter_type/filter_values/output_tsv_path, more than 300 filter_values, its parent directory does not exist, acknowledge_default_limit_override and row_limit were not given together, row_limit exceeded the 5,000 hard cap, or session_id/flow_id were missing from the calling context. marketo.export_path_refused: the path is not absolute, not a .tsv, or not contained under any operator-configured export_allowed_roots entry (an empty export_allowed_roots refuses every export by default). Vendor-side faults (marketo.auth_failed, marketo.permission_denied, marketo.partition_access_denied, marketo.object_not_found, marketo.rate_limited) can NOT surface here -- they only appear later, in check_marketo_job_status's error field, once the background worker actually calls Marketo.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: marketo.invalid_params: read describe_lead_fields.searchable_fields and use an exact returned field name; if it is null (the instance's describe response omits the field), fall back to a well-known standard filter_type such as id or email rather than guessing. For the override pair, pass BOTH acknowledge_default_limit_override=true and an explicit row_limit, or neither (for the 500-lead default); a row_limit above 5,000 is refused outright, not clamped. marketo.export_path_refused: pass an ABSOLUTE path ending in .tsv under a configured workspace root; if export_allowed_roots is empty, add the operator's export directory to the marketo_plugin config and reload it. Once dispatch succeeds, poll check_marketo_job_status(job_id) -- if THAT reports an error, its guidance covers the vendor-side classes (auth, permission, partition, rate limit).
